feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector roles: it presents a clear leadership profile, solid progression, and relevant platform/analytics expertise. Impact is good, but it would be stronger with more quantified outcomes, less repetition across skills sections, and tighter formatting consistency.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline, summary, and experience align well around digital platform leadership, governance, communications systems, and public-sector impact.  
- Credibility and progression: long tenure at NACo with steady advancement supports leadership claims and domain depth.  
- Good use of scale indicators: examples like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers” add substance.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than results; include gains in traffic, engagement, efficiency, adoption, cost savings, or campaign performance.  
- Reduce duplication and improve structure: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to make the CV leaner and easier to scan.  
- Fix stylistic inconsistencies: “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is unusual; punctuation/list style varies (e.g., “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “A2/Learning” is awkward—use “A2 (learning)”); “10×20-foot” may be clearer as “10 x 20-foot.” No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and public-sector focus. It reads well, but it’s slightly dense and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and recent experience bullets.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten to one sharper value proposition and foreground scale/results: “Senior digital leader with 12+ years modernizing high-volume public-sector communications platforms, governance, and content operations.”
- Replace the generic “Leads…” list with a more distinctive summary tied to recent work: “Delivers enterprise web modernization, analytics ecosystems, editorial workflows, multimedia operations, and AI-enabled search/content experiences.”
- Consider adding one scale marker from recent roles for impact, e.g., “10,000+ page website,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ internal publishers.”
- Standardize style: use either “AI-enabled” consistently everywhere and consider “public sector” vs. “public-sector” consistently across the CV.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Repeats themes already covered in the subtitle and Core Competencies; the intro should summarize, not restate lists.
- “Multimedia production” and “editorial systems” are reinforced extensively in Work Experience, so keep them brief here.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-level leadership strengths will make it feel more distinct and executive-level.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and simplify wording: “Enterprise web modernization,” “Digital governance and editorial operations,” “Analytics, reporting, and insight systems.”
- Replace broad or repetitive items with sharper, more senior language: “Cross-channel communications leadership” instead of “Multi-channel communications operations.”
- Consider a tighter version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight systems • Cross-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Keep “public-sector” hyphenation consistent and use “and” vs. “&” consistently across the CV.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “AI-enabled search,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “multimedia/livestream” are already repeated in the header and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with both the header and multiple NACo roles.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and repeats themes already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing and adding parallel structure will make it more scannable and distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro like “Selected recent projects” and format each item as a concise title + outcome-focused sentence.
- Use parallel verbs and cleaner phrasing: “Built,” “Led,” “Developed,” “Produced”; change “10×20-foot” to “10 x 20-foot” for style consistency.
- Emphasize what was distinctive or high-value in each project (e.g., AI chat for bill discovery, Drupal 10 modular architecture, conference activation tied to web experience).
- Trim stacked descriptors: “hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search” is strong, but simplify where possible for readability.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series substantially overlap with recent NACo roles; keep this section more portfolio-like and less repetitive of job bullets.
- “Built/Developed” repeats across all entries; vary wording slightly to avoid monotony.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a broad service list rather than a high-impact consulting entry. Tighten around 3–4 highest-value contributions and add outcomes, scope, or named deliverables where possible.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper positioning line: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform improvement, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery initiatives.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance into one impact-focused bullet: “Improved cross-channel communications operations by refining publishing workflows, analytics, and governance across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make technical delivery more outcome-led: “Built Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content components, and downloadable member toolkits for public-facing initiatives.”
- Add measurable signals if available: number of sites/pages supported, campaign launches, reduction in publishing time, search/discovery improvements, stakeholder groups served.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Current wording overlaps with prior NACo roles on governance, analytics, and digital operations; emphasize consultant-level advisory scope and new AI/search work.
- “CMS development/front-end implementation/technical troubleshooting” may duplicate skills sections unless tied to a specific business result.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, multimedia production, and budget/team operations.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground impact: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page site to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable results where missing: growth in email/social engagement, reduction in external production costs after studio launch, reporting speed/visibility improvements from analytics stack expansion.
- Combine softer operational bullets for concision: “Established governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning systems to improve consistency and execution across digital channels.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video-programming language may duplicate older NACo entries unless framed here as building the in-house studio/capability.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like a bridge role than a distinct step up. Emphasize what changed under your ownership: scale, cadence, cross-team coordination, and channel development.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to focus on operational ownership and scope: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, improving editorial coordination and advocacy content delivery.”
- Tighten bullets and make them outcome-led: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Clarify the video impact: “Launched and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger line: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and cross-department coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations…” overlaps with the Director of Digital Media entry; use “managed” or “oversaw daily execution” here.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the prior role; frame this entry as scaling/formalizing the program, not originating it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value leadership capabilities not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, executive-level language tied to recent work:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy campaigns
- Audience strategy & content planning
- Consider swapping “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” for “Campaign and storytelling strategy” if you want less repetition with other sections.
- Keep wording parallel and concise; avoid nouns like “messaging” and “planning” repeated elsewhere unless they signal a distinct strength.
- If space allows, make one line more outcome-oriented, e.g., “Enterprise web strategy for high-volume public-sector platforms.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” is already covered in Work Experience and Core Competencies.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. This topline item should emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities tied to enterprise web modernization and delivery.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, with the strongest/recentest items first.
- Suggested rewrite: “Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery • Website modernization and platform migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and content discovery”
- Consider dropping older/lower-signal platforms here (e.g., WordPress, SharePoint) unless they are central to target roles.
- If space allows, replace one generic item with a scale cue from recent work, e.g., “Drupal modernization for 10,000+ page public-sector site.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills strategic/capability-based and leave full platform inventory to Technical + IT.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies; vary wording to “AI-enabled search and content discovery.”

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for a senior digital leader, but it overlaps heavily with “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize strategic application and executive value, not just tool names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Analytics strategy & reporting” rather than leading with platforms.
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy & reporting • KPI framework design • Executive dashboarding and leadership reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio and Microsoft Clarity • SEO, UX and performance analysis”
- Keep only the most decision-oriented items here; move lower-level terms like individual tools to Technical + IT if space is tight.
- If possible, align with proven impact from recent roles by implying business use: “decision support,” “performance monitoring,” or “optimization insights.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Avoid repeating the exact same tool stack elsewhere unless this section is intentionally more strategic.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the Core Competencies line and multiple NACo roles. Make it more distinctive by emphasizing production environment depth and delivery scope rather than broad labels.

Suggested edit
- Replace generic terms with sharper, senior-level phrasing: “Broadcast-quality video production,” “livestream and hybrid event delivery,” “PTZ/multi-camera direction,” “studio build-out and operations.”
- Group related skills to improve scanability: “Video production, editing, and studio operations • Livestream, hybrid, and virtual event delivery • PTZ and multi-camera systems.”
- If accurate, add scale or complexity signals: “broadcast-quality,” “recurring advocacy programming,” “in-house studio workflows,” or “high-visibility member events.”
- Consider a tighter rewrite: “Broadcast-quality video production and editing • Livestream, hybrid, and virtual event delivery • PTZ and multi-camera studio operations”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrase verbatim.
- “Studio operations” and video production are already evidenced in recent NACo roles, so this skills line should stay concise and complementary.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either add context on level of use or be tightened to emphasize the most relevant, recent platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize current/recent platforms first: **Drupal • SharePoint • Power Pages • WordPress • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add proficiency context rather than just listing tools, e.g. **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • SharePoint/Power Pages (Microsoft ecosystem) • WordPress • GitHub Pages**
- Consider renaming to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing and consistency with the rest of the CV.
- If you want stronger impact, replace the standalone list with a more outcome-linked line: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; campaign microsites) • SharePoint • Power Pages • WordPress • GitHub Pages**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; keep the stronger version and trim the other.
- Drupal impact is already well evidenced in recent experience, so avoid repeating it elsewhere without added context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical range, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools you actively use in recent work and group items more strategically.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Front-end & implementation:** HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery • **Integration & tagging:** API integrations, Google Tag Manager • **Edge & deployment:** Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the rest of the CV uses version-specific naming; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner.
- If accurate, replace broad terms with stronger specifics tied to recent work, e.g., “REST API integrations,” “CI/CD workflows,” or “serverless edge scripting.”
- If space allows elsewhere, move one proof point into recent experience instead of this list, such as GTM implementation, Workers-based functionality, or GitHub Actions automation.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Workflow automation” in Topline Skills may also overlap with GitHub Actions unless differentiated.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too broad and mixes automation platforms with project/collaboration tools. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Split by function and tighten wording: “Automation & Workflow: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier” and move Jira/Asana/Basecamp/Trello to a “Project & Work Management” item; Slack/Teams belong under “Collaboration Tools.”
- Prioritize tools tied to recent impact; keep Airtable, Power Automate, and Zapier first since they best support your systems/governance narrative.
- If accurate, add a light qualifier for depth: “Airtable (system design), Power Automate (Microsoft workflows), Zapier (cross-platform automations).”
- Suggested rewrite: “Automation & Workflow: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier | Work Management: Jira • Asana • Trello • Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack • Microsoft Teams”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- Slack/Teams are generic unless central to a measurable achievement elsewhere.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This is relevant to the candidate’s recent leadership in email operations, but it reads as a bare vendor list and misses the strategic/enterprise angle shown elsewhere. It should signal scale and platform ownership without repeating newsletter details already covered in work experience.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email, CRM & Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten and modernize the list: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights & Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add a light qualifier for scope rather than features, e.g. **enterprise email automation, member communications, audience engagement**
- Keep it platform-focused only; let the work experience carry outcomes like audience size and newsletter cadence

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding “email newsletters,” “tens of thousands,” or campaign execution language here; that is already covered in the 2022–2024 and 2018–2022 roles.
- “Engagement” overlaps with broader multi-channel communications language elsewhere, so “CRM & Engagement Platforms” is clearer and more specific.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” In a technical section, it should read as a sharper capabilities list and emphasize higher-value analytics infrastructure over broad marketing terms.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by strategic weight and recency: “BigQuery • GA4 • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • KPI reporting • SEO analysis • A/B testing”
- Replace vague “Dashboarding” with a more specific capability such as “KPI reporting” or “Executive dashboards.”
- Consider tightening the title to “Analytics & Optimization” since “Data” is broad and unsupported by deeper data-engineering tools.
- If accurate, upgrade one item to reflect implementation depth: e.g., “GA4 implementation,” “Analytics reporting,” or “Experimentation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly identical to “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; differentiate this section as tools + methods, while Topline Skills stays higher-level.
- Avoid repeating all five tools elsewhere unless tied to outcomes in the 2022–2024 NACo role.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with clearer scope and any available metrics.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-stage team building and hands-on delivery: “Promoted through two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Add concrete outputs if you can: number of livestreams/video episodes produced, size/timing of website refresh, channels supported, or team size.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce generic terms like “high-impact” and “strengthening workflows.”
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted through two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations. Contributed to a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and helped formalize day-to-day publishing workflows. Provided direct guidance to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; differentiate this as the earlier launch/build phase.
- Workflow/governance language also appears in later roles; keep this entry focused on implementation, not leadership.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/multimedia. Emphasize the podcast launch and any concrete project outputs, while trimming generic support language.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the standout achievement: “Coordinated innovation and policy research initiatives for NACo programs; launched the organization’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a clearer outcome-focused line, e.g., “Produced multimedia and digital content that supported member programs and policy communications.”
- If possible, add scale or results: number of episodes, featured stakeholders, audience growth, or how the podcast supported advocacy/member engagement.
- Keep this entry shorter than later NACo roles since those show greater leadership and scope.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with the 2015–2018 and 2018–2024 NACo entries; avoid repeating generic multimedia language.
- Don’t overstate team leadership here, since stronger management evidence appears in later roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too generic and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies and “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” in Topline Skills. In a senior CV, this section should stay tool-focused and avoid repeating broader capabilities already proven in recent roles.

Suggested edit
- Rename/refocus as software + platforms only: “Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator”
- If you want to keep production systems, make them more technical and concise: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Livestream studio systems”
- Drop “Podcast production” unless you can specify a platform/tool (e.g., Riverside, Libsyn, Pro Tools); otherwise it reads as a responsibility, not a technical skill.
- Consider ordering by strongest/recent relevance: “Premiere Pro • Audition • Livestream studio systems • Photoshop • Illustrator”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Livestream studio workflows” duplicates Topline Skills (“Livestreaming,” “Studio operations,” “Hybrid and virtual event production”).
- “Podcast production” is already supported in older experience; avoid repeating it here unless tied to a named tool/platform.
